Gemini 4 Hydrogen just built a horse out of Minecraft blocks and called it a day 

Same prompt, 4 AI workflows: a horse galloping through water.

Same horse, same lake, but the gap between the results is brutal 

The horse racing department is cooked

🥇 Fable 5.2 → low-poly horse in a low-poly world, huge water splashes and a gallop that actually looks heavy

🥈 Gemini 4 Carbon → warm sunset canyon, smooth horse and a very cinematic look

🥉 GPT-6 Astra → beautiful mountains and forest, but a low-poly horse inside a realistic world

💀 Gemini 4 Hydrogen → somehow a black voxel horse that looks like it escaped from Minecraft

The interesting part isn’t the horse

It’s how the legs, the splashes and the reflections work together

Pretty lighting can’t save you if the water doesn’t react to every hoof

Fable made the whole scene feel like one world, while Astra’s horse and background look like they belong to different games

At this point AI doesn’t need better horses

It needs to learn how water works 

Which horse would you pick?

Ex-OpenAI @cdngdev reveals how he used an approach called program learning to get 250 AI agents to collaboratively build the algorithm behind his 1:1 recreation of Earth in Minecraft:

"If I'd wanted to do a full model to actually do this conversion, like a diffusion model, it would be incredibly expensive."

"Instead, I decided to go with a more algorithmic approach that was defined by the models, but still a learned approach."

"I took first Astra, then Claude, and picked a set of a ton of locations around the world, a training and a test set, where the models could basically build out their generator."

"I spawned 250 agents to go to every single one of these training areas and modify the scripts to recreate it in Minecraft. All these agents are collaboratively creating this converter script."

"Before deep learning, we did this thing called symbolic AI, where humans would try to program weights almost into these models, and this was really bad and not scalable because you’re bottlenecked by humans."

"Now that we have agents that are able to write these weights, I can almost think of the code that it’s running as weights for the model, because I can’t understand what the code is doing."
